sections.content: Travel narratives depend on the contrast between background and completed events. The imperfecto sets the scene or describes an ongoing situation, while the indefinido moves the story forward through completed events. The pluscuamperfecto places one completed event before another past event. Good narratives combine these forms rather than using one past tense for every sentence.

items.spanish: Cuando llegamos a la estación, había mucha gente.
items.english: When we arrived at the station, there were a lot of people.

items.spanish: El tren salió con retraso porque había una avería.
items.english: The train left late because there was a breakdown.
While we were waiting, they announced the cancellation.

items.spanish: Ya habíamos comprado otro billete cuando llegó el mensaje.
items.english: We had already bought another ticket when the message arrived.

sections.content: Ask what each event is doing in the story: setting the scene, advancing the narrative, or showing what had already happened.
